01 / Before you start

Check your disc dump.

Shinka currently targets the European multilingual release, Digimon World 2003, disc ID SLES-03936. The US Digimon World 3 and Japanese releases are not supported by this build.

For the current setup, keep the .cue file and its matching .bin file together. The CUE describes the disc; the BIN contains its data. Select the CUE in Shinka setup; it locates and checks the matching BIN.

Choose English in the game for Shinka's expanded menus. An ISO, CHD or multi-BIN dump is not a supported installer input; renaming its extension will not convert it.

A folder with both files

My disc dump/
  game.cue
  game.bin

Your filenames can be different. Keep the name inside the CUE matched to the BIN it references.

How is the version checked?

The build verifies the entire BIN before preparing game code. The currently supported SHA-1 is:

457cb233349ba841e03b33d8060f8fbcadd45cb3

A different hash is rejected. Even the right title or region alone does not guarantee a match.

02 / Install & prepare

Choose your disc. Prepare once. Play.

Setup downloads about 200 MiB of preparation tools and needs at least 6 GiB of free space. It prepares the game on your computer; you do not need to install Python, Visual Studio or separate DLLs.

  1. Run the installer

    Download the EXE above and install for your Windows account. Open Shinka Setup from the Start menu.

  2. Select your CUE

    Use the disc picker to choose your CUE file. Leave it and its BIN where they are: Shinka remembers their location and reads the original files without modifying them.

  3. Choose whether to import a card

    To start fresh, leave the emulator search unchecked. To continue a DuckStation save, follow the card-import steps below before preparing.

  4. Prepare Shinka

    Select Prepare Shinka and allow several minutes for the first setup. Progress shows the current stage. If preparation fails, use Open preparation logs for details, fix the reported issue and retry.

  5. Play

    Once setup reports ready, select Play. Use the Shinka shortcut for later launches. OpenBIOS is included; a separate console BIOS is not required for this installer.

Original music is included. Alternate soundtrack setup remains separate. This preview has native battle/movie code and interpreter fallback for other overlays; performance can differ from the development build shown in some demos.

Optional / Developer route

Prefer to build from source?

The Windows build and launch guide covers prerequisites, pinned dependencies, BIOS options and manual launch commands. These steps are an alternative to the installer.

03 / Optional

Keep your progress.

Close DuckStation before importing. In Shinka Setup, tick Search for existing emulator data (DuckStation). Select a memory card from the results, or use Choose folder… or Choose card file… for a custom location.

Choose slot 1 or 2 and confirm that DuckStation is closed. Setup copies the selected card into a new Shinka save profile and verifies it. Your original card stays untouched. A DuckStation savestate (.sav) cannot be imported.

In the game, select Continue to load the copied card. Use Open saves in setup to find the active profile and back it up. Reinstalling or uninstalling Shinka preserves player data under %LOCALAPPDATA%/Shinka.

Manual card import and backups ↗

04 / First session

You're at the title screen.

Start or continue

At language selection, press Start to confirm. Use Start for a new game or Continue for a memory-card save.

Once in the world, open the Start menu. SETTINGS contains EXP, encounters, screen view, soundtrack and battle animation speed. Original music works without an extra music pack; alternate palettes need local music-pack setup.

Controller setup ↗

If something gets stuck

Find the next step.

The window never opens

Open Shinka Setup from the Start menu and check its status. If it offers Repair Shinka, run that first. Use Open preparation logs to read any error. Launch through the Shinka shortcut rather than an executable copied out of its folder.

The disc is rejected

Check the release and file format above. The build accepts one specific BIN hash. It will reject another region, a modified dump or a different image layout. Keep the error message; do not bypass the check or rename another format to BIN.

Continue cannot find my save

Use Open saves to check the active profile. It should contain the imported card in the slot you selected. Load it through the game's Continue option. If a save folder was moved or disconnected, restore it before launching; setup will not silently create a blank replacement.

DIGIVOLUTIONS or SETTINGS is missing

Choose English in the game. The installer enables the expanded menu. For a source build, use -EvolutionJournal on the first launch as described in the build guide.

I moved my disc folder

Keep the CUE and BIN together. Open Shinka Setup, pick the CUE in its new location and run setup again. Shinka checks the new path while retaining the prepared game and save profile.
